## Welcome

This course teaches the statistical foundations behind modern crop genomics — mixed models, multivariate statistics, Bayesian inference, machine learning, multi-omics integration — and the delivery skills that turn analysis into tools: interactive web apps, databases, and HPC pipelines.

Every module runs on **real, public datasets** from crops that matter to Canadian agriculture: prairie yield trials, CIMMYT wheat, pea diversity panels, canola RNA-seq, and maize hybrids.

::: {.callout-note}
## Who this is for
Bioinformaticians and geneticists who *use* statistics daily and want to understand **how the methods actually work** — and statisticians who want realistic genomic case studies.
:::

## Weekly outline

| Week | Topic | Dataset | Key packages |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | Biostatistics, R, and friends | — | tidyverse |
| 1 | Linear & mixed models, spatial trials | `agridat` prairie trials | sommer, lme4 |
| 2 | PCA, PLS-DA, clustering | Pea GWAS panel | mixOmics, FactoMineR |
| 3 | Bayesian regression & MCMC | `BGLR::wheat` (CIMMYT) | BGLR, coda |
| 4 | Penalized regression, RF, boosting | wheat + `DT_technow` maize | tidymodels, xgboost |
| 5 | RNA-seq DE, WGCNA, MOFA2 | Canola GEO counts | DESeq2, MOFA2 |
| 6 | Interactive apps | Weeks 2–4 outputs | shiny, plotly |
| 7 | SQL & REST APIs | Weeks 2–4 outputs | RSQLite, plumber |
| 8 | SLURM, Snakemake, containers | Week 4 pipeline | snakemake |

## How to use this course

1. Complete [Setup](setup.qmd) — one command installs everything.
2. Work each week's page top-to-bottom; every page ends with exercises.
3. Each `.qmd` is downloadable (code button, top right) to run locally.
